validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, well-documented, correctly classified. This is a PNGRB-authorised common-carrier natural gas transmission pipeline built by Reliance Gas Pipelines Limited (RGPL) to evacuate CBM gas from RIL's Sohagpur (SP-East/SP-West) coal-bed-methane blocks in Shahdol district, MP, to a tie-in with GAIL's HVJ trunk network at Phulpur, UP. Independent corroboration (5 separate origins, none GEM-derived): (1) PNGRB's own monthly regulator inventory (NGPL-MIS Report, May 2026 edition) lists it by name under 'OPERATIONAL COMMON CARRIER PIPELINE' #16, entity=RGPL; (2) RGPL's own operator website has a dedicated technical page for 'Shahdol-Phulpur Gas Pipeline (SHPPL)'; (3) a signed RGPL-to-PNGRB regulatory filing (Access Code Regulations questionnaire, 27 Jun 2019, RGPL letterhead) names the pipeline and confirms RGPL as the authorized entity; (4) Business Standard (independent press, 9 Jun 2017) reported RGPL 'laid a 302 km Shahdol Phulpur Gas Pipeline' connecting the CBM fields to GAIL's HVJ network; (5) CARE Ratings (credit-rating agency, Oct 2024 press release on RGPL's bank facilities) describes 'SHPPL's pipeline, housed under RGPL' in detail including FY24 utilisation and volumes. PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas are correct -- this is a trunk transmission line, not a gathering/process line (the RIL Gas Gathering Station at Shahdol is a separate upstream facility that feeds INTO this pipeline). No duplicate risk found against the 35-pipeline India-gas operating roster -- no other row references Shahdol, Sohagpur, or this CBM system. One data-quality aside (not a sheet defect): gem.wiki's own cite_note-3 (an EOI PDF at pngrb.gov.in/pdf/eoi/ng/eoi9/feb-14-EOI-9.pdf) is mislabeled on the wiki page -- the actual PDF content is an unrelated EOI (customer list totalling ~90 mmscmd, no mention of Shahdol or Phulpur), not the Shahdol-Phulpur EOI its wiki link-text claims. Not used as a source here; flagging only because the guidance says to verify wiki leads live.

validity.recommendation: Correct Owner1 from 'Reliance Industries Ltd' to 'Reliance Gas Pipelines Limited (RGPL)' -- keep Owner1%=100.00% (RIL's stake in RGPL, not in the asset directly), and optionally note in ResearcherNotes that RGPL is a wholly-owned RIL subsidiary.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's Owner1 is 'Reliance Industries Ltd' 100%. Four independent sources agree the pipeline is legally owned and operated by a distinct subsidiary, Reliance Gas Pipelines Limited (RGPL) -- not directly by RIL: (1) PNGRB's NGPL-MIS report lists the authorised Entity as 'RGPL' with the legend 'RGPL = Reliance Gas Pipelines Limited'; (2) RGPL's own regulatory filing to PNGRB (27 Jun 2019) is on RGPL letterhead, signed by RGPL's Director, and states 'Name of the authorized entity: Reliance Gas Pipeline Limited (RGPL)'; (3) Business Standard (2017): 'Reliance Gas Pipelines Limited (RGPL) a wholly owned subsidiary of RIL, laid a 302 km Shahdol Phulpur Gas Pipeline...'; (4) CARE Ratings (2024): 'RGPL, a wholly owned subsidiary of RIL' and 'SHPPL's pipeline, housed under RGPL'. So RIL's 100% ultimate ownership is not wrong as a fact, but the entity that holds the PNGRB authorisation and legally owns/operates the asset is RGPL, a step removed from RIL. An earlier company name for the same/related entity appears in a 2015 trade-press piece as 'Reliance Gas Transportation Infrastructure Corporation Limited (RGTIL)' -- 'the Gas transmission arm of Reliance Industries Limited' -- which received the pipeline license; by the 2017-2024 sources it is consistently RGPL, so RGTIL looks like an earlier/alternate name for the same corporate transmission arm, not a separate owner (kept out of the Owner field to avoid asserting an unverified corporate-history claim).

validity.recommendation: No change recommended, but note the authorised-vs-built length split in ResearcherNotes: LengthKnown=312 km matches PNGRB's AUTHORISED length exactly; the physically built/operating pipe is consistently reported at 302-304 km across independent sources.
validity.researcher_notes: LengthKnown=312.00 km matches PNGRB's NGPL-MIS report 'Authorised Length (KM)' column for Shahdol-Phulpur (RGPL, authorised 11.07.2013) exactly -- 312 km. However, the same PNGRB report's 'Operating Length (KM)' column for this pipeline reads 304 km, and RGPL's own site independently describes 'SHPPL system is a 16 diameter x 304 km main pipeline.' Business Standard (2017, at commissioning) reported RGPL 'laid a 302 km Shahdol Phulpur Gas Pipeline.' So there is a real, well-corroborated 8-10 km gap between the AUTHORISED length (312, which the sheet uses) and the BUILT/OPERATING length reported by the regulator and the operator itself (302-304). This is not a sourcing error on GEM's part -- 312 is a real, PNGRB-documented figure -- but if LengthKnown is meant to track built physical pipe (GEM's usual convention) rather than the authorised/nameplate length, 304 km (the figure both PNGRB's own 'Operating Length' column and RGPL's technical description converge on) would be the more defensible value. Flagging as a caveat rather than changing the value, since 312 is independently sourced and the discrepancy is a documented authorised-vs-built distinction, not a fabrication or unit error.

Capacity=3.50 MMSCMD is corroborated by three independent origins agreeing on the exact same figure: (1) PNGRB's NGPL-MIS report, Authorised Capacity column = 3.5 MMSCMD (Design/Determined capacity also 3.5, i.e. no authorised-vs-design gap here, unlike some other India rows); (2) RGPL's own 2019 regulatory filing to PNGRB states verbatim 'System capacity of the pipeline is 3.5 MMSCMD'; (3) CARE Ratings' 2024 press release: pipeline capacity 'at 3.5 million metric standard cubic metre per day (mmscmd)', also reporting FY24 utilisation of 17% (vs PNGRB's most recent monthly reading of 26% for May 2026 -- both plausible snapshots of a pipeline whose utilisation has fluctuated with new-well drilling, not a conflict). FuelSource='Sohagpur CBM Fields' is also confirmed and precise -- RGPL's site and Business Standard both name the specific source as the Sohagpur East (SP-E) / Sohagpur West (SP-W) CBM blocks operated by RIL in Shahdol district.

validity.recommendation: no action needed on StartYear1; do not substitute the 2013 PNGRB authorisation date for this
validity.researcher_notes: StartYear1=2017 is consistent with Business Standard's contemporaneous (9 Jun 2017) reporting that RIL's Sohagpur CBM production 'is currently being supplied for commissioning the Shahdol Phulpur Pipeline (SHPPL)' and that RGPL 'laid' the pipeline connecting the fields to GAIL's HVJ network -- i.e. 2017 is when the pipeline was being brought into service, matching CBM production start (24 Mar 2017). This is a single strong contemporaneous source (medium tier on its own), not independently duplicated elsewhere with an explicit year, so treating as confirmed-with-caveat rather than fully closing it out. Flagging explicitly per the country guidance: PNGRB's 11.07.2013 date on this pipeline is an AUTHORISATION date, not a commissioning date, and should not be substituted for StartYear1 -- the sheet correctly does not do this.

fills.researcher_notes: Diameter was blank in the sheet (one of only 10/75 India gas rows with a diameter sourced). RGPL's own operator technical page states 'SHPPL system is a 16 diameter x 304 km main pipeline.' Single first-party operator source (no second independent source found specifying pipe diameter -- PNGRB's regulator report does not carry diameter, and no PNGRB tender/bid document specific to this pipeline was found), so tier=medium rather than high; recommend staging as a fill rather than leaving unresolved given the source is the pipeline's own operator.

summary: P0953 (Shahdol-Phulpur) is a real, well-corroborated RGPL common-carrier CBM-evacuation pipeline (5 independent sources incl. the PNGRB regulator, RGPL's own site/filings, Business Standard, CARE Ratings); Capacity (3.5 MMSCMD), FuelSource, PipelineType and StartYear1=2017 all confirmed. One attribution concern staged: Owner1 should be Reliance Gas Pipelines Limited (RGPL), not Reliance Industries Ltd directly, per PNGRB/RGPL/press/CARE agreement (RIL is RGPL's 100% parent, not the direct asset owner). One spec caveat noted (not changed): LengthKnown=312 km matches PNGRB's authorised length exactly, but the built/operating pipe is consistently reported at 302-304 km by PNGRB's own 'Operating Length' column, RGPL's site, and 2017 press. One fill staged: Diameter=16 in (RGPL's own site, single-source/medium tier).
